summary: This exercise is a self-directed ESG integration case study in which students select a real company and apply sustainable finance frameworks to analyse its business model, stakeholder relationships, material ESG factors, impact, non-financial reporting quality, and environmental/social value creation.

question_types.description: Students describe the chosen company's business model, customer value proposition, and sources of competitive advantage, testing the ability to identify and articulate how a firm creates and captures economic value.

Students identify the company's purpose, map key stakeholders using a structured impact tool, and assess externalities and ethical dilemmas, testing skills in stakeholder theory and corporate sustainability thinking.

Students determine the most material ESG factors for the company and evaluate each factor's effect on competitive position and value drivers using a structured table, testing the ability to apply ESG materiality frameworks in a corporate context.

Students map the company's activities to relevant UN Sustainable Development Goals and score its impact on the criteria of materiality, intentionality, and transformational potential, testing knowledge of impact investing frameworks.

Students critically evaluate the company's sustainability and annual reports against principles such as strategic focus, connectivity, materiality, and reliability by assigning scores on a 1–10 scale, testing the ability to assess integrated reporting standards.

Students quantify environmental and/or social value generated by the company using shadow prices and self-made assumptions, testing the ability to apply monetary valuation techniques to non-financial impacts.
